properties.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
properties.description: Head shrine of Inari with 10,000+ vermilion torii gates forming tunnels up Mount Inari. Foxes (kitsune) guard the shrine.
properties.modernStatus: Active Shinto shrine, most visited in Japan

properties.name: Ise Grand Shrine (Ise Jingū)
properties.description: Japan's most sacred Shinto shrine, dedicated to Amaterasu. Rebuilt every 20 years in an eternal cycle of renewal spanning 1,300+ years.
properties.modernStatus: Active shrine, rebuilt every 20 years (most recent: 2013)

properties.name: Itsukushima Shrine (Floating Torii)
properties.description: Shinto shrine with its iconic 'floating' torii gate rising from the Inland Sea. Built over water to separate the sacred from the profane.

properties.name: Izumo Taisha (Grand Shrine)
properties.description: Second most important Shinto shrine, dedicated to Ōkuninushi (god of nation-building and marriage). All gods gather here in October.

properties.name: Mount Fuji (Fujisan)
properties.description: Japan's highest peak (3,776m) and most sacred mountain. Home of Konohanasakuya-hime, goddess of flowering. Pilgrimage to the summit is a spiritual practice.
properties.modernStatus: UNESCO World Heritage Site, active pilgrimage

properties.name: Tōdai-ji (Great Eastern Temple)
properties.description: Houses the world's largest bronze Buddha (15m tall). The wooden hall is the world's largest wooden structure, rebuilt smaller than the 752 original.
properties.modernStatus: UNESCO World Heritage Site, active Buddhist temple
